The plan for selling on your DigitalOcean account

This page is the storefront — the part customers see. Live selling needs one more piece behind it: a small backend service on DigitalOcean that creates Stripe Checkout sessions, confirms payments by webhook, and writes orders to a database. That backend is not built yet. Here is the complete plan for “all of it,” in order, so nothing is a surprise.

1 · Host the store

App Platform

Runs this storefront for you — no server to patch. It rebuilds and redeploys every time you update the store.

2 · Take payments

Backend + Stripe

A small web service (the piece still to build) talks to Stripe: it creates each Checkout session, receives Stripe’s payment webhook, and only then marks an order paid. A static page alone cannot do this.

3 · Store the files

Spaces

Object storage for cover art and product photos, served fast through its built-in CDN.

4 · Keep the orders

Managed PostgreSQL

A managed database the backend writes orders, customers, and inventory to — with automatic backups turned on.

1

Host this storefront

In DigitalOcean, go to Apps → Create App and deploy this page as a static site named pilikia-store (from a GitHub repo holding these files). This part is ready today.

2

Add your domain

In the app’s Settings → Domains, add the domain you want customers to use and follow the DNS step it shows. HTTPS is automatic — don’t turn it off.

3

Create a Spaces bucket

Go to Spaces → Create, name it pilikia-store-files, and upload the cover art and product images from this page’s assets folder. Point the store’s image links at the bucket when you move them.

4

Build the backend service

Add a second component to the same App Platform app: a small web service with endpoints to create a Stripe Checkout session from the cart, receive Stripe’s checkout.session.completed webhook, and save the paid order. This is custom code — it’s the main build still ahead.

5

Add the database + Stripe keys

Go to Databases → Create → PostgreSQL and attach it to the backend (not to this static page). Add your Stripe keys to the backend’s environment variables as STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Never paste a secret key into this page or into chat.

6

Test, then launch

With the backend deployed, place a test order in Stripe test mode, confirm the webhook writes the order to the database, then switch Stripe to live mode and do one small real purchase and refund before sharing your domain.

Where things stand: This storefront — products, real DistroKid Direct prices, cart, and order summary — is done and works on this page. Each product's Buy Now button takes PayPal and debit/credit card payments now. A full cart checkout still needs the backend service in Step 4, deployed on your DigitalOcean account with your Stripe keys. Until that backend exists, use the order summary from the cart, and the same merch stays buyable through your DistroKid Direct store.
